title: The 'little piano girl of East Liberty' and the Pittsburgh parties
summary: From 6 to 14 she played the parties of wealthy Pittsburgh families, including the Mellons, and her brother-in-law took her to theatres to listen.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: When did you start playing with any regularity anywhere? Was it during this period?

From the age of 6 until I was 14 I was all over the city playing. I played for the Mellons. I became the little piano girl of East Liberty and anytime anybody was having a party or anything they'd say, "Well, let's get the little piano girl." So by this time I was among nothing but the wealthy people of Pittsburgh, playing for their parties. The chauffeur would pick me up or my stepfather, Fletcher Burley, would take me. He would take me to parties like for the Mellons and my brother-in-law, Hugh Floyd, would take me to theatres to keep my ears open and listen to musicians. Sometimes I would go to sleep and he'd throw me over his shoulder and bring me home.
So you were getting real training?
